title: Sensitive logs intake: prioritization ladder & legal routing for redaction, retention, export
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: define a deterministic intake and prioritization ladder for customer requests that involve sensitive logs (PII, regulated identifiers, or security telemetry) and the downstream handling: redaction, retention adjustments, and audit exports. This ticket scopes the prioritized decision matrix, routing rules to Legal/Compliance, required evidence for exec approvals, and per-customer runbooks for safe execution. We will produce: 1) a triage ladder mapping risk categories to response paths and SLAs; 2) routing matrix (self-serve -> PM -> Legal -> Engineering) with automation triggers; 3) templates for customer-facing responses and internal runbooks; 4) a checklist for engineering change requests (RBAC, encryption, k-anonymization), and 5) observability/QA tests for regression on redaction pipelines. Out of scope: bulk data migration tooling and on-prem install packaging (handled by Private infra team).
comments: 2026-03-02 — Initial intake meeting with Support and CS. Common customer asks: timestamp retention extension, PII removal retroactively, and CSV audit exports for compliance. Action: gather 10 representative requests (shared drive: https://drive.redwood/example-sensitive-requests).

2026-03-04 — Legal (Maria Gonzalez) reviewed draft ladder; recommended adding a ‘data subject rights’ path and requiring explicit DSR evidence for PII redaction. Legal asked for retention variance justification for >90 days. See Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood/sensitive-logs-ladder

2026-03-06 — Eng architectural readout (Jonas Meyer): redaction in-flight vs retrospective differs in complexity; retrospective scrubbing requires safe backfill orchestration and KV-cache invalidation for affected models. Engineering requests gating on a scoped API cadence and clear SLAs before implementation.

2026-03-09 — Design provided customer response templates and a short FAQ for CS. Decision: implement a staged rollout—pilot with 3 enterprise customers and a canary procedure before wide release. Raised follow-up ticket to create automation for evidence collection (PM-68045).
acceptance_criteria: A documented prioritization ladder that maps request types (retention change, export, PII redaction, legal hold) to risk tiers and required approvals.
A routing matrix with automated triggers and clear ownership for each step (Support -> PM -> Legal -> Eng), including SLA per tier.
Customer-facing response templates and internal runbooks for the 4 most common request patterns.
A checklist for Eng changes that enumerates tests, RBAC reviews, encryption/KMS considerations, and rollback procedure.
Pilot plan and rollback criteria defined; pilot runbook scheduled with 3 named customers and monitoring dashboards.
Instrumented metrics and alerts for redaction regressions (false negatives/positives) and export integrity checks with dashboards linked.
Security sign-off from Legal and Security teams recorded in Confluence before engineering work begins.
